### Verdict
**Yes**, termination of the given TRS can be established from the rules alone (no extra axioms, guards, side-conditions, or structural assumptions beyond the free term algebra generated by the signature implicitly present in the rules).

### Termination argument
The signature consists of the function symbols appearing in the rules: unary \(\mathsf{exec\_walk\_weight}\), nullary \(\mathsf{nil}\) and \(\mathsf{zero}\), binary \(\mathsf{cons}\), \(\mathsf{add}\) and \(\mathsf{app}\).  The only symbol that possesses rewrite rules is \(\mathsf{exec\_walk\_weight}\); \(\mathsf{add}\) and \(\mathsf{app}\) are uninterpreted.  Consequently every redex is an instance of one of the three left-hand sides.

Define a simple measure on ground terms by
\[
\mu(t)\;=\;\text{the multiset of the sizes (number of function symbols) of all second arguments of occurrences of \(\mathsf{exec\_walk\_weight}\) in \(t\)}.
\]
Multisets of natural numbers are well-ordered by the multiset extension of \(>\) on \(\mathbb{N}\).

- Rule 1 rewrites \(\mathsf{exec\_walk\_weight}(w,\mathsf{nil})\) to the constant \(\mathsf{zero}\).  The multiset \(\mu\) loses one element and therefore strictly decreases.
- Rule 2 rewrites \(\mathsf{exec\_walk\_weight}(w,\mathsf{cons}(x,\mathsf{nil}))\) to \(\mathsf{zero}\).  Again \(\mu\) loses one element and decreases.
- Rule 3 rewrites
  \[
  \mathsf{exec\_walk\_weight}(w,\mathsf{cons}(x,\mathsf{cons}(y,xs)))
  \]
  to
  \[
  \mathsf{add}(\mathsf{app}(\mathsf{app}(w,x),y),\;\mathsf{exec\_walk\_weight}(w,\mathsf{cons}(y,xs))).
  \]
  The second argument of the unique recursive call is a proper subterm of the second argument of the redex, hence has strictly smaller size.  No new occurrence of \(\mathsf{exec\_walk\_weight}\) is introduced by \(\mathsf{add}\) or \(\mathsf{app}\).  All other subterms (the instances of \(w,x,y,xs\)) already occur in the left-hand side, so they contribute exactly the same multiset elements on both sides.  Consequently \(\mu\) decreases.

Every rewrite step therefore decreases the measure \(\mu\).  An infinite rewrite sequence is impossible.

(The same conclusion is reached by the recursive path order with precedence \(\mathsf{exec\_walk\_weight}>\mathsf{add}>\mathsf{app}>\ldots\) and lexicographic status, or by the polynomial interpretation that maps \(\mathsf{exec\_walk\_weight}(w,l)\) to \(2\cdot|l|\), \(\mathsf{cons}\) to successor, and every other symbol to the sum of its arguments; both orderings are definable from the rules alone.)

All three rules have been examined; no additional hypotheses were required.
